**(i)** Two independent events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A) = \frac{1}{5}$ and $P(B) = \frac{3}{20}$.

Find

Question 1 (ii) : le sujet imprime « vacinated » et « vacine » (fautes d'orthographe) ; l'énoncé est transcrit avec l'orthographe « vaccinated » / « vaccine ». La notation $P(A/B)$ du sujet désigne la probabilité conditionnelle $P(A \mid B)$.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Here $P(A/B)$ means the conditional probability $P(A \mid B)$. For any events with $P(B) > 0$,

$$P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}.$$

Because $A$ and $B$ are independent, $P(A \cap B) = P(A)\,P(B)$, so

$$P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A)\,P(B)}{P(B)} = P(A) = \frac{1}{5}.$$

**$P(A \mid B) = \dfrac{1}{5} = 0.2$** (knowing that $B$ has occurred does not change the probability of $A$).

For independent events the multiplication rule gives

$$P(A \cap B) = P(A)\,P(B) = \frac{1}{5} \times \frac{3}{20} = \frac{3}{100}.$$

**$P(A \cap B) = \dfrac{3}{100} = 0.03$.**

By the addition rule,

$$P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B) = \frac{1}{5} + \frac{3}{20} - \frac{3}{100} = \frac{20 + 15 - 3}{100} = \frac{32}{100}.$$

**$P(A \cup B) = \dfrac{8}{25} = 0.32$.**

Check with the complement: $P(A' \cap B') = P(A')\,P(B') = \frac{4}{5} \times \frac{17}{20} = \frac{68}{100}$, and $1 - 0.68 = 0.32$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**(ii)** 60% of the population of a certain country have been vaccinated against COVID-19. During an outbreak of the COVID-19 epidemic, $\frac{1}{5}$ of those who had taken the vaccine were infected and $\frac{2}{3}$ of those who had not taken the vaccine were infected.

Find the probability that an individual selected at random from this country

(d) is infected.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $V$ be the event "the individual has taken the vaccine" and $I$ the event "the individual is infected". From the data

$$P(V) = 0.6,\quad P(V') = 0.4,\quad P(I \mid V) = \frac{1}{5},\quad P(I \mid V') = \frac{2}{3}.$$

(Tree diagram: first branches $V$ and $V'$, then $I$ and $I'$ on each.) The individual is infected through exactly one of the two disjoint routes $V \cap I$ or $V' \cap I$, so by the law of total probability

$$P(I) = P(V)\,P(I \mid V) + P(V')\,P(I \mid V') = 0.6 \times \frac{1}{5} + 0.4 \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{3}{25} + \frac{4}{15} = \frac{9}{75} + \frac{20}{75}.$$

**$P(I) = \dfrac{29}{75} \approx 0.387$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (e) is infected or had taken the vaccine.
questions.corrige_markdown:
We want $P(I \cup V) = P(I) + P(V) - P(I \cap V)$, with

$$P(I \cap V) = P(V)\,P(I \mid V) = 0.6 \times \frac{1}{5} = \frac{3}{25}.$$

$$P(I \cup V) = \frac{29}{75} + \frac{3}{5} - \frac{3}{25} = \frac{29}{75} + \frac{45}{75} - \frac{9}{75} = \frac{65}{75}.$$

**$P(I \cup V) = \dfrac{13}{15} \approx 0.867$.**

Check with the complement: not infected and not vaccinated has probability $P(V')\,P(I' \mid V') = 0.4 \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{15}$, and $1 - \frac{2}{15} = \frac{13}{15}$.
